title: Bar da Praia do Carvalhal
vimeoName: Module 4 — Bar da Praia do Carvalhal

segments.text: On the sand of the Costa Vicentina, minutes from Craveiral,
is the beach our guests use most.
The easiest access on this stretch of coast, the one families
prefer.
That is where Bar da Praia do Carvalhal is,
and the shortest definition I can give you is this:
the beach bar is the Craveiral philosophy in flip-flops.
Easier, looser, more informal,
never more careless.
There is a temptation in this unit, and it is worth naming.
Because the register is more informal, it is easy to let the standard
slide with it.
They are not the same thing.
Informal means no linen tablecloth and no formal
address.
It does not mean a badly washed glass, a toilet nobody is
checking, or a 20-minute wait with nobody saying anything.
The register changes, the standard does not.
If you keep one line from this module, keep that one.
And there is something the bar team needs to see clearly.
To anyone walking off that beach and into the bar, you are
Craveiral.
Many of those people have never slept on the farm and perhaps never will.
That glass, that plate, that good morning, is the only sample
of the brand they will get.
A good hour in that bar sells room nights we will
never be able to attribute to anyone.
A bad hour closes doors we never knew we closed.
The menu follows the same logic as the house: honest, simple,
with an origin.
Fish from this coast, products from the region, wines we
know the source of, and whatever the farm can send.
The chain is told here as it is told at the farm table.
Only instead of a sentence at the table,
it is a sentence at the counter in five seconds.
"This is from our garden, 20 minutes
from here."
Five seconds.
Nobody is in a hurry for a lecture on the beach, but everyone warms
to something true.
The bar is also where the surf lessons start, booked through
reception.
And here is the rhythm of the perfect day, which I want you to know by
heart because it is the best recommendation we have.
Morning on the farm, lunch and afternoon at Carvalhal,
dinner under the stars back home.
Recommending the beach is not sending the guest out of the business,
it is moving them inside it.
And when reception says this on arrival,
the guest feels somebody thought about their day.
That is hospitality, not selling.
Two operational demands the beach makes and the farm does not.
The first is time.
On the beach, people get hungry at unpredictable hours and
have short patience under the sun.
A wait time communicated,
"It is 20 minutes. Shall I bring you water meanwhile?"
settles 90% of complaints before they exist.
What generates a complaint is not waiting.
It is waiting without information.
The second is sun and water.
Shade, cold water, toilets checked hourly,
attention to children and older people at midday.
Wellbeing on the beach is mostly reducing physical discomfort
nobody puts into words.
And because we are on a Costa Vicentina beach inside a protected
area,
there is a coherence that is not negotiable.
We do not let plastic loose in the wind.
We collect what is ours and some of what is not.
We close the day with the sand in front of us better than we found
it.
A bar that lives off the beauty of that coast and dirties it, is the
most visible contradiction this group can produce.
And it is visible to hundreds of people a day, not to an
annual audit. Your module in three things.
You change the register,
never the standard.
To anyone coming out of that water, you are the whole of Craveiral.
And what you serve has an origin you can tell in five seconds.
The rest is what you already know how to do.
Be present,
see before you are asked,
and treat that counter as if it were your own living room,
because it is.
In the next module, the shop, the territory condensed and
portable.
